scores.accuracy_concern: The three-month framing needs its source stated: Lawrence 2004 found recovery of basic daily activities took about 3 months and of household and community activities about 6 months after major abdominal surgery in people aged 60 and over, not for all operations; Fried 2002 figures come from 226 seriously ill US patients and should carry that population.
scores.sharpen: Anchor the three-month question to Lawrence 2004 and use it as the single public post on surgical consent, choosing it over C07-21 or C07-25 so the argument about recovery of daily life appears once per audience.

scores.accuracy_concern: 'Before it helps anyone' overstates the concept: time to benefit is the time until a set absolute benefit is reached (Lee 2013 about 10 years to prevent 1 cancer death per 1000 screened; Yourman 2021 about 2.5 years to prevent 1 major cardiovascular event per 100 treated, in 50 to 75 year olds; Deardorff 2022 about 12 months to prevent 1 non-vertebral fracture per 100 women), and benefit builds gradually before that; trial populations were younger or fitter than many of the readers.
scores.sharpen: Replace 'before it helps anyone' with 'before the benefit shows up in trials' and show only two or three verified examples, each with its outcome, denominator and trial age range written beside it.

scores.accuracy_concern: In the UK, NICE NG136 targets were not derived from SPRINT (NICE did not adopt the SPRINT target), so 'the trial behind lower blood pressure targets' fits US and European guidance, not NICE; SPRINT's standing-pressure exclusion was below 110 mmHg after 1 minute standing, and SPRINT used unattended automated measurement that reads lower than routine clinic measurement.
scores.sharpen: Say which targets SPRINT informed, add the unattended-measurement point, and close on a practical test: would this person have been eligible for the trial, and what is their standing pressure?

scores.accuracy_concern: Evidence that medicines stopped in hospital are restarted because the reason was not recorded is thin and may rest on local audits; Kripalani 2007 covers discharge communication deficits in general and is nearly 20 years old, so the causal chain (missing reason leads to restart) needs a direct source or should be presented as reasoning.
scores.sharpen: Merge with C07-16 into one 'record the reason' teaching post, or move it to C06 or C15, and find a direct source on post-discharge restarting before relying on it.

scores.accuracy_concern: State verified ASPREE figures: 19,114 participants, median 4.7 years, no difference in disability-free survival, major haemorrhage about 3.8% versus 2.8%, all-cause mortality 5.9% versus 5.2% with the authors' caution that the mortality finding was unexpected; PREVENTABLE may not have reported by September 2026, so describe it only as ongoing unless verified.
scores.sharpen: Lead with the outcome choice in plain words, give the bleeding result as N in 100 over about 5 years, and keep the line for people taking aspirin after a heart attack or stroke prominent on the visual as well as the caption.

scores.accuracy_concern: DAH30 validation (Myles 2017) was in an Australian surgical cohort and home-time measures correlate with other outcomes; the scenario of a service keeping mortality low while patients spend much of the next month in hospital must stay an illustrative example, not a finding about any service.
scores.sharpen: Tie it to a treatment decision (days at home as the figure to ask about before high-risk surgery) or move it to C20, and add one verified figure on how DAH30 tracks disability.

scores.accuracy_concern: Contact-day evidence comes from cancer trials (for example the CO.17 secondary analysis); do not transfer its proportion of days to other treatments, and treat the dialysis schedule (three sessions a week of about four hours) as typical in-centre practice that varies with home and incremental dialysis.
scores.sharpen: Give one verified contact-days figure from the cancer literature as the anchor and name the carer's time explicitly, keeping dialysis as a generic example only.

scores.values_concern: Make clear the choice belongs to the person, or is a best-interests decision if they lack capacity, and is never a default adopted to save staff time.
scores.accuracy_concern: Robbins 2008 compared chin-down posture with two thickened liquids and had no thin-liquid control, so it cannot show that thickened fluids fail to reduce pneumonia; say instead that evidence that thickened fluids prevent pneumonia is limited. The RCP 2021 careful hand feeding guidance centres on advanced dementia and progressive conditions.
scores.sharpen: Replace the Robbins claim with 'there is little evidence that thickened fluids prevent pneumonia' and give families one request: a documented eating and drinking with acknowledged risks plan agreed with the speech and language therapist.

scores.accuracy_concern: The Serious Illness Care Program trial was in US oncology outpatients and did not improve its primary outcomes (goal-concordant care and peacefulness); the reduction in anxiety and depression symptoms was a secondary outcome and should be labelled as such.
scores.sharpen: Open with a concrete clinical moment rather than a principle, and state plainly that the trial missed its main outcomes, so the post teaches the sequence without overselling the guide.

scores.accuracy_concern: Check NG136 wording: the standing measurement is after at least 1 minute standing, a significant drop is a systolic fall of 20 mmHg or more, and treating to the standing reading applies to people with a postural drop or symptoms, not to everyone aged 80 and over; NICE web pages could not be opened here, so use an opened copy or the BMJ guideline summary.
scores.sharpen: Open with the consequence (a seated reading above target in someone whose pressure falls on standing) and state the 20 mmHg definition and 1-minute timing on the flow diagram.

scores.accuracy_concern: Which services can view the Key Information Summary needs an opened source (official web pages could not be opened here); Scottish terminology has moved from anticipatory care planning to future care planning, and ReSPECT is used in many but not all UK areas, so check current names and coverage.
scores.sharpen: Use the current Scottish term alongside KIS and ReSPECT, and add one sentence on exactly what to ask the GP to record, whether the wish is for more treatment or less.

scores.accuracy_concern: 'Almost every 78-year-old, whatever their cholesterol' needs documented QRISK3 outputs; for women with very favourable profiles the score may sit close to 10% in the mid seventies, so 'most' is safer unless verified. NG238 also allows statins below 10% by informed preference, so the threshold is not a strict gate in either direction.
scores.sharpen: Build the chart from reproducible QRISK3 outputs with inputs listed, and name the three things to weigh instead: time to benefit, other illnesses and frailty, and what the person wants.

scores.accuracy_concern: Some medicines should not be stopped abruptly (steroids, beta-blockers, antiepileptics, some antidepressants), so 'a medicine can usually be stopped and restarted' needs qualifying; the GMC end-of-life guidance dates from 2010 with a 2022 update.
scores.sharpen: Give one concrete example in each column and a tapering caveat, or fold it into C07-26 as that post's public version.

scores.values_concern: Frame combining or cancelling appointments as reducing burden with the person's agreement, not as rationing access.
scores.accuracy_concern: Quote NG56 accurately on assessing treatment burden and agreeing who coordinates care; links between treatment burden and poorer adherence or quality of life are observational and should be described as associations.
scores.sharpen: Add one verified figure on appointment load in multimorbidity, and select either this or C07-07 rather than both, since they make the same time-burden argument for different audiences.

scores.accuracy_concern: 'White-coat effect is common in older people' needs a specific source; 'treatment decisions are safer with home readings' is a reasonable inference, not a trial finding; state the NICE home method (paired readings twice daily for at least 4, ideally 7, days, discarding the first day) from an opened copy.
scores.sharpen: Add a specifically geriatric point (the lower home target for people 80 and over and the postural drop), or drop it in favour of C07-10 to avoid a third blood pressure post.

scores.accuracy_concern: The 'unwise decision' principle is section 1(4) of the Mental Capacity Act 2005 (England and Wales); the Adults with Incapacity (Scotland) Act 2000 principles are different (benefit, least restrictive option, past and present wishes, consultation, residual capacity), and the Scottish unwise-decision point comes from its Code of Practice, so do not attribute it to the Act's principles.
scores.sharpen: Separate the English and Scottish legal bases correctly and use one example of a correctable factor (a hearing aid not in) to show how the fuller note protects both the decision and access to care.

scores.accuracy_concern: Programme ages differ by nation (England breast to the 71st birthday with self-referral after; England and Scotland bowel 50 to 74 with kits on request after); NHS and Cancer Research UK web pages could not be opened here, so verify ages, self-referral routes and the share of cancers diagnosed at 75 and over (about a third) from an opened document.
scores.sharpen: Add one sentence that requesting screening after invitations stop is itself a choice to weigh with the GP, so the post separates 'report symptoms at any age' from 'keep screening' without pushing self-referral on everyone.

scores.values_concern: Avoiding life-expectancy wording must not turn into withholding prognosis from people who ask for it.
scores.accuracy_concern: Schoenborn 2017 was a qualitative study of about 40 US older adults; the phrasing preferences come from a separate US national survey (Schoenborn 2018, JAMA Oncology research letter), so quote its most and least preferred explanations exactly and state the US population.
scores.sharpen: Show the survey's preferred and least-preferred phrasings verbatim on the card, and add a line that honest prognosis should still be offered when the person wants it.

scores.accuracy_concern: ONS period life expectancy at 80 is roughly 9 to 10 years for women and 8 to 9 for men, but the exact figures need an opened ONS source (ONS pages could not be opened here); the Walter and Covinsky quartiles come from 1990s US life tables and must not be merged with UK figures; the anti-ageism position is ethical judgement plus data and should be marked as judgement.
scores.sharpen: Use current opened period figures, keep the dated US quartiles clearly separate, and close on a question to ask: which parts of my health, rather than my age, change this decision?

scores.accuracy_concern: The 2021 BPLTTC individual participant meta-analysis appears to show relative effects that weaken with age, with no clear reduction in the 85 and over group (hazard ratio close to 1, wide uncertainty), so the 85 versus 55 example uses the age where the relative effect is least certain; CTT 2019 found a trend to smaller proportional reductions at older ages; HYVET's primary stroke reduction (about 30%) was of borderline significance, while death and heart failure fell clearly.
scores.sharpen: Use the 75 to 84 group where relative effects held, say plainly that relative effects look smaller at the oldest ages, and correct the HYVET stroke claim before the arithmetic point can stand.

scores.accuracy_concern: The Montgomery materiality test (para 87) is quoted correctly, but McCulloch v Forth Valley Health Board [2023] UKSC 26 held that which alternatives are 'reasonable' is judged by the professional practice test, so the duty to discuss no treatment should rest on GMC guidance; 'falls short of what Montgomery requires' is a legal interpretation to soften.
scores.sharpen: Soften the legal conclusion, cite McCulloch alongside Montgomery, and choose between this and C07-01 so the surgical-consent argument is not made twice.

scores.accuracy_concern: Verify OPTIMISE figures: 569 randomised; systolic below 150 mmHg at 12 weeks in about 86% (reduction) versus 88% (usual care); about two thirds of the reduction group stayed on the reduced regimen; GPs selected participants they judged suitable for reduction, which limits generalisation.
scores.sharpen: Open with the question families ask (do all these blood pressure tablets still need taking?) and put the 86 versus 88 in 100 figures, the two-thirds figure and the 12-week limit in consecutive sentences.

scores.accuracy_concern: GAP70+ enrolled 718 patients; grade 3 to 5 toxicity was about 51% versus 71%; the intervention was a geriatric assessment summary plus management recommendations given to oncologists, so the effect belongs to the whole package, in people with advanced cancer starting a high-risk regimen; ASCO guidance is US.
scores.sharpen: Give the toxicity result as about 51 versus 71 in 100 and add a sentence on how to ask for a geriatric assessment in UK services where it is not routine.

scores.values_concern: Present conservative kidney care as active care and the person's choice, never as a verdict that frail people's time on dialysis is poorly spent.
scores.accuracy_concern: Kurella Tamura 2009 studied US nursing home residents (about 58% had died and 13% had kept their previous function at 12 months), not older people generally; survival comparisons of dialysis and conservative care are observational and confounded, so 'adds little time' must become 'observational studies suggest smaller survival differences' in named groups.
scores.sharpen: State the Kurella Tamura population in the same sentence as its figures, replace 'adds little time' with the observational finding for a named group, and list what conservative care actively provides.

scores.accuracy_concern: Evidence for Best Case/Worst Case is mainly pre-post and simulation work in the US; check whether the multisite stepped-wedge trial has reported and what it found before saying the tool improves decisions.
scores.sharpen: Fold it into C07-01 as the clinician-facing version, or verify the trial result first and lead with the drawn two-bar graphic.

scores.accuracy_concern: Chang 2021 was a before-and-after quality improvement study in three US ICUs in people with advanced medical illness, not a randomised trial and not specific to older people; the claim that time-limited trials prevent premature withdrawal is the rationale, not a measured finding.
scores.sharpen: Open with the vague plan it replaces ('let's see how it goes') and label the Chang evidence as a US ICU before-and-after study in the caption.

scores.accuracy_concern: Beach and Morrison 2002 used case scenarios given to physicians (a vignette survey), not observed orders; the BMA, Resuscitation Council UK and RCN guidance concerns DNACPR specifically, so the intensive care opening needs its own source or should be reframed around CPR or ReSPECT.
scores.sharpen: Reframe the opening around a DNACPR or ReSPECT decision where the guidance applies, describe Beach and Morrison as a scenario survey, and keep the long 'continues' column as the visual.

scores.accuracy_concern: StatinWISE used six blinded 2-month periods in random order, not alternating months; 200 were randomised and 151 completed, mean age about 69; general practice cannot routinely offer a blinded placebo, so the practical option is an unblinded stop and restart, which is a weaker test.
scores.sharpen: Describe the design correctly, say that a blinded trial is not routinely available so an unblinded rechallenge is the practical version, and consider moving it to C06.

scores.accuracy_concern: Lipska 2015 used US NHANES 2001 to 2010 data; check the exact proportions of people in poor health with HbA1c below 7% and of those on insulin or sulfonylureas; the hypoglycaemia link with falls is observational; the UKPDS legacy benefit was in newly diagnosed middle-aged people, not frail older adults.
scores.sharpen: Add the specific action (review HbA1c and drug class together, reduce the sulfonylurea or insulin first) with the UK frailty guidance target range, and state the UKPDS population and time frame.

scores.accuracy_concern: IST-3 enrolled 3035 people, of whom 1617 (53%) were over 80, across both arms, so say 'enrolled', not 'treated'; eligibility still depends on time since onset, brain imaging and pre-stroke function; confirm IST-3 is still the largest thrombolysis trial given recent tenecteplase trials; check the 2023 guideline wording on age.
scores.sharpen: Change 'treated' to 'enrolled', add one line that eligibility depends on timing and scans rather than age, and keep the 999 instruction as the close.

scores.accuracy_concern: Tinetti 2019 was a non-randomised comparison in one Connecticut health system; report which outcomes improved (treatment burden score, medicines or tasks stopped) and which did not change, and avoid implying generalisability to UK primary care.
scores.sharpen: Put the two questions in plain words as the visual, state the non-randomised design and the outcomes that did not change, or merge with C07-14 as one treatment-burden post.

scores.values_concern: Present deactivation as a choice some people will make and others will not, without implying it is expected near the end of life.
scores.accuracy_concern: Figures for shocks in the last days of life vary by study (Goldstein 2004; Kinch Westerdahl 2014) and need verifying before any number is used; check whether the 2013 BHF guidance has been updated; keep the claim to the shock function, since pacing continues after deactivation.
scores.sharpen: Keep the tone about planning rather than expectation, verify one figure on shocks near death for the caption, and add who to ask (the heart failure, cardiology or device clinic team).

scores.accuracy_concern: 3D trial: 1546 patients in 33 practices; no clear difference in EQ-5D-5L at 15 months; improved patient-centred care measures; only about half of intervention patients received the full planned reviews (check the process evaluation); do not suggest the quality of life measure was wrong without evidence.
scores.sharpen: Name one patient-reported measure that improved and the proportion who received the full reviews, and consider C20 for it, since its main point is how to read a null trial.

allocation_reason: All 33 clear 36 and 19 score 45 or more with no disqualifying flag; even after moving the ones better placed in C06, C19, C13 or C20, at least 14 strong C07 posts remain, and proportional care is central to the brief and missing from the earlier collection.
balance_note: The top 14 split into 5 public (32, 17, 07, 24, 11), 5 both (27, 05, 30, 23, 02) and 4 practitioner (29, 12, 03, 18), with 'do not undertreat because of age' posts (30, 23, 17, 27) balancing the 'less treatment' ones. Overlaps to resolve at allocation: 32, 27 and 11 with C19; 29, 22 and 28 with C06; 08 with C13; 06 and 33 with C20; 16 and 09 with C09. Within this set, take at most two of the blood pressure group (03, 10, 15, 22), one or two of the surgical consent group (01, 21, 25) and one of the time-burden pair (07, 14). If C19 takes 32 and 27, the next C07 choices are 01, 26, 10 and 06. Note that the weights add to 11, so the real maximum total is 55, not 50.
